{{Short description|Belarusian theoretical physicist}}
'''Ilya Mark Nemenman''' (born January 8, 1975, in [[Minsk]], Belarus) is a theoretical physicist at [[Emory University]], where he is a Winship Distinguished Research Professor of Physics and Biology. He is known for his studies of information processing in biological systems and for developing coarse-grained models of these systems.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.physics.emory.edu/home/people/faculty/nemenman-ilya.html|title=Ilya Nemenman|website=www.physics.emory.edu}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] for "his contributions to theoretical biological physics, especially information processing in a variety of living systems, and for the development of coarse-grained modeling methods of such systems".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://biomed.emory.edu/news-events/news-releases/2016/10/nemenman-made-aps-fellow.html|title=Nemenman Made Fellow of the American Physical Society {{!}} GDBBS {{!}} Emory University|website=biomed.emory.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-12-20|archive-date=2017-10-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171014184747/http://biomed.emory.edu/news-events/news-releases/2016/10/nemenman-made-aps-fellow.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is a [[Simons Foundation|Simons Investigator]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/grant/simons-investigators/?tab=awardees&filter_disciplines=theoretical-physics-in-life-sciences&filter_years=2021|title=Simons Investigators in Mathematics and Physical Sciences|access-date=2022-03-09}}</ref> and [[James S. McDonnell Foundation]] Complex Systems Scholar.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jsmf.org/grants/2012022/|title=JSMF Funded Grants|access-date=2022-03-09}}</ref> He also served in the Chair Line of the Division of Biological Physics of the American Physical Society, from 2013 to 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/units/dbp/governance/committees/index.cfm|title=APS Division of Biological Physics Committees}}</ref> Nemenman also was a founder of the q-bio conference, and is a general member of the [[Aspen Center for Physics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aspenphys.org/aboutus/governance/board/members.php|title=Aspen Center for Physics Board Members|access-date=2017-12-30|archive-date=2017-12-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171230114723/https://www.aspenphys.org/aboutus/governance/board/members.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Life ==
Ilya Nemenman is the son of [[Mark Nemenman]], a Soviet computer scientist. He studied physics at the [[Belarusian State University]] before moving to the US to complete his BS in physics and math at [[Santa Clara University]]. He studied for his master's degree in physics at [[San Francisco State University]]. He studied for his PhD under [[William Bialek|Bill Bialek]] at [[Princeton University]], and graduated in 2000. He then completed postdoctoral research at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] and [[Columbia University]] before starting work at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]]. Finally, in 2009, he moved to join the faculty at Emory University.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.scu.edu/media/college-of-arts-and-sciences/physics/newsletter/MARCH-23-Newsletter.pdf|title=Catching Up with alumni: Updates from some of our graduates|newspaper=Department of Physics Newsletter|publisher=Santa Clara University|date=March 2011}}</ref> He has 3 children.
